title: Where the official numbers live
subject: Money

text: IRS.gov is the source. Everything else is a retelling.
A retelling can be useful. It is not the number you file with.
Standard deduction and brackets: the IRS news release on inflation adjustments, and Publication 17.
EITC: the Earned Income Tax Credit page and the EITC Assistant. Free File: the Free File page on IRS.gov, not a company's homepage.
Type the address. IRS.gov/FreeFile. IRS.gov/EITC. IRS.gov/VITA.
Do not click a search ad. Ads buy the words 'free file' and 'IRS'. The real page is the one whose address is irs.gov.
What an official page looks like
It is on irs.gov. It names a tax year. It has a form number or a publication number if it is giving a rule.
Publication 17 is the plain-language book. The form instructions are the filing rules. A news release announces a change. A blog announces nothing.
You want the Free File income limit. Where do you start?

choices.label: IRS.gov/FreeFile, typed in, not a search ad.
The first result for 'free tax filing'.
A preparer's homepage that says IRS approved.

text: irs.gov for the number. Publication 17 and the form instructions for the rule. The EITC Assistant to check a credit.
If the address is not irs.gov, it is someone else's summary.
